rulings.challenge_claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative denies that any first-person or discourse-restart marker separates 4:14 from 4:15-16, but Eccl.4.15 opens with the first-person raiti-observation verb ("I saw") -- the same device this row's own observed_substrate_signals cites and that sibling rows in this cluster treat as a legitimate discourse-restart marker -- so the stated warrant against splitting at 4:14|4:15 is factually inaccurate on the bytes.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed directly from verse_map_oshb.json: Eccl.4.15 opens רָאִ֨יתִי֙ -- verse-initial, first-person, and ASYNDETIC (no waw connective at all). Cross-checked against eccl_device_inventory.json's frame_seams.raiti_observations (18 refs total: ['Eccl.1.14', 'Eccl.2.13', 'Eccl.2.24', 'Eccl.3.10', 'Eccl.3.16', 'Eccl.3.22', 'Eccl.4.4', 'Eccl.4.15', 'Eccl.5.12', 'Eccl.5.17', 'Eccl.6.1', 'Eccl.7.15', 'Eccl.8.9', 'Eccl.8.10', 'Eccl.8.17', 'Eccl.9.13', 'Eccl.10.5', 'Eccl.10.7']); re-deriving the verse-initial split at skeleton tier gives exactly 4 bare-form sites (['Eccl.1.14', 'Eccl.3.10', 'Eccl.4.15', 'Eccl.10.7']), 4 waw-prefixed sites (['Eccl.2.13', 'Eccl.3.22', 'Eccl.4.4', 'Eccl.8.17']), and 10 non-initial occurrences -- Eccl.4.15 is one of only 4 bare/asyndetic sites book-wide. This same cluster already treats the WAW-PREFIXED member of the same device as a legitimate discourse-restart driver twice: at Eccl.3.22 (וְרָאִ֗יתִי, P01-017's own closing verdict) and at Eccl.4.4 (וְרָאִ֨יתִֽי אֲנִ֜י, which P01-018's rejected_alternative names as 'a clean restart point' and P01-019's boundary_rationale treats as a genuine formal shift). Applied consistently, the bare/asyndetic form at 4:15 is at least as strong a restart signal as either waw-prefixed instance already used as a driver, not an absent one. The row's OWN observed_substrate_signals field lists frame_seams.raiti_observations -- the only raiti site inside this row's own Eccl.4.13-Eccl.4.16 span is 4:15 -- so the row registers the marker as an observed signal and then denies its existence in the very next field (strongest_rejected_alternative: 'no first-person or discourse-restart marker separates them'). This is a confirmed, byte-grounded self-contradiction within the row itself, independent of either primary's packet. Additionally confirmed: Eccl.4.15 carries tachat-hashemesh -- one of MT ch 4's 4 sites (['Eccl.4.1', 'Eccl.4.3', 'Eccl.4.7', 'Eccl.4.15']), a formula this row also declares in observed_substrate_signals -- reinforcing 4:15 as a formal observation-opener rather than a bare continuation of 4:14's narration. NEW FINDING (independent of both primaries): the row's boundary_rationale already gestures at the correct counter-argument without landing it -- 'the closing verdict at 4:16 depends grammatically on the same narrated succession the whole unit describes' -- but never names the actual textual mechanism. Eccl.4.15's phrase הַיֶּ֣לֶד הַשֵּׁנִ֔י ('the youth, the second/other one') carries the definite article on both words, while Eccl.4.13's יֶ֥לֶד ('a youth') is indefinite -- a classic Hebrew indefinite-then-definite anaphoric chain: 4:15's definite 'the youth' presupposes and cannot be read apart from the youth first introduced at 4:13. This is confirmed, independent, byte-grounded support for keeping Eccl.4.13-Eccl.4.16 as one row that does NOT depend on denying the 4:15 raiti marker exists -- so the marker's presence, once honestly conceded, does not by itself force a boundary reversal at 4:14|4:15; it forces a grounds correction. Neither primary's packet names this definiteness-shift mechanism.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite strongest_rejected_alternative in one edit (both primaries' items share this single cure): (1) concede that Eccl.4.15 opens with the bare/asyndetic raiti-observation verb -- the same device this row's own observed_substrate_signals already cites, and, being asyndetic rather than waw-prefixed, at least as strong a restart signal as the two waw-prefixed instances (3:22, 4:4) this same cluster already treats as drivers; (2) replace the false 'no marker separates them' claim with the actual warrant: Eccl.4.15's definite 'the second youth' is anaphoric on the indefinite 'a youth' first introduced at Eccl.4.13, so the restart marker is present but grammatically overridden by referential dependency, and the closing verdict at 4:16 depends on that same narrated succession. Cure test: strongest_rejected_alternative must name the Eccl.4.15 marker explicitly (byte tier, asyndetic form specified) rather than deny it, and must ground the retained boundary in the definiteness-shift/antecedent chain rather than in the marker's absence -- this is the test the original failed twice over (self-contradicting its own declared signal, and omitting the one argument -- referential dependency -- that actually supports its conclusion). This is a grounds correction: the existing span (Eccl.4.13-Eccl.4.16, one row) and unit_type are not, on this record, shown to require reversal.
rulings.convergence_note: SAME underlying defect as the OL item on this row (both target the identical false 'no marker' claim and both independently note the row's own self-contradiction with its declared raiti signal); OL's packet additionally supplies the bare-vs-waw-prefixed strength comparison and the tachat-hashemesh reinforcement, both confirmed here and folded into this ruling's shared grounds. One remedy cures both.
